Read all six counterexample steps and all 13 suppliers. Checked char k not 2 and nonzero nonsquare a, irreducibility/separability, the rank-two basis and differential calculation, the mu_2 Hopf maps and action, and both inverse coordinate maps x -> tx, y -> x, t -> x/y, x -> y. The relation is the entire structure-map kernel pair, with both projections finite locally free by the basis and involution; invariants are k by evaluation at +/-1. Thus the finite-relation theorem represents X/G by Spec k while X(k)/G(k) is empty. The identity class gives a matching family over X -> Spec k; the ratio y/x is defined because a is a unit and has square 1, yet no section descends in the naive presheaf. This is a genuine sheafification counterexample, not a failure of representability. The reader correctly removed the nonexistent orbit-map/basepoint kernel-pair citation and supplied the basis/involution proof. Accepted repair with confidence 1. Empty test scheme is singleton, the chosen X is nonempty, and a=0, squares and characteristic 2 are explicitly excluded. AC is inherited from the quotient and etale suppliers. Stacks 39.20.1/39.23.9 and Milne pp.139-143 were checked for the conventions and route. The reader proof repair is retained; the carrier is amended only by refreshing its exact F2 action-definition quotation after the supplier clarification.

Read all six steps and all 12 suppliers, including the complete connected-group supplier proof. Connected smooth separated G is geometrically integral; separatedness is Milne Proposition 1.22, complete proof at p.12. Therefore the orbit map is dominant between irreducible classical varieties and the exact closed-point generic-fibre theorem applies. Every nonempty finite-type fibre over algebraically closed k has a k-point, and left translation identifies it with H scheme-theoretically; no reducedness of H is used, and reduction preserves underlying dimension. Compare on a nonempty open with a closed point to obtain dim G = dim H + dim O. The proper closed boundary in the irreducible closure has strictly smaller dimension and is G-stable, so every boundary orbit is smaller; finite descent of nonnegative dimensions gives a closed orbit. The union-of-orbits assertion is in the stated classical closed-point convention. Checked trivial and zero-dimensional groups, H=G, trivial action and empty boundary; x excludes empty X. AC is explicit for the suppliers/closed points. Milne 1.66,5.23,7.4-7.6,A.72 at pp.27-28,104,139-140,586 and Brion 1.11 complete argument were read. Confirmed refuter:15:4 and corrected Brion to printed p.4; no mathematical body or interface change. Confidence 1.

Read all eight verification steps and all 34 dependency interfaces, including current GL_n and representation definitions with their AC/rank-zero qualifications. T is the closed diagonal-matrix subgroup with invertible entries over every test ring. Field-valued pairs of distinct lines have independent frames; the universal two line bundles on M=Y minus Delta have wedge determinant nonzero in every residue field, hence a unit on affine frame charts. The resulting matrix a gives the actual scheme isomorphism U x T -> q^-1(U), with inverse a(q(g))^-1 g; thus q is faithfully flat locally of finite presentation, and all test-scheme kernel pairs are genuine torus cosets. The criterion identifies the fppf quotient, not only field points. The dimension calculation is over the algebraic closure and connectedness is checked by the nonempty determinant open in A4. K-point surjectivity and injectivity hold for every extension field K, with finite choices of two vectors. Accepted the reader determinant/trivialization repair (short nonfatal gap); amended the Example and step 5.1 because the fibre over a nonrational point is over kappa(y), not k. In particular the generic fibre is A1_{k(t)}, not A1_k as a k-scheme. The revised statement quantifies over every point, preserving the full content. No direct item consumer or other item reference to this example was found; no further hop is needed. Milne 7.18 is the general quotient method; Example 7.19 concerns the upper triangular subgroup and is contextual, not evidence for the diagonal-torus identification. Brion 1.12/1.16 is likewise contextual; the specific quotient and all fibre formulas were checked directly. Both repairs have confidence 1.
